# OpenCode V2 Plugins and Hooks

How OpenCode V2 plugins load, which hook points exist, and where a plugin can
enforce something a permission glob cannot express. The permission layer is in
[permissions.md](permissions.md); the Claude Code comparison is in
[vs-claude-code.md](vs-claude-code.md).

> Provenance: `@opencode/plugin@2.2.7` type definitions and
> `@opencode/schema@2.2.7` config schema (npm registry); `envsitter-guard@0.1.1`
> README and source, whose author states the plugin was verified end to end
> against OpenCode 2.0.32 and 2.1.0. The official pages
> <https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/plugins> and
> <https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/config> were **not** reachable from the sandbox
> this doc was written in (fetch-service off). Claims marked "third-party" below
> rest on those packages, not on an official page read here.

## Plugin shape

A V2 plugin is a default export with an `id` and a `setup` function:

```js
export default {
  id: "my-plugin",
  async setup(ctx) {
    await ctx.tool.hook("execute.before", (event) => {
      if (event.tool === "shell" && event.input.command.includes("git push")) {
        throw new Error("blocked");
      }
    });
  },
};
```

`setup` may return a cleanup function. Hooks registered during `setup` attach to
the plugin's scope, so unloading the plugin disposes them. The package also
exports `define(plugin)` as an identity helper and an Effect-flavored API
(`@opencode/plugin/effect`) that returns `Effect.Effect<void, never, Scope>`
instead of a Promise.

## Loading locations

Two mechanisms exist. The config schema has a top-level `plugins` array whose
entries are either a package specifier string or `{ package, options }`
(`@opencode/schema@2.2.7`, `dist/config/plugin.d.ts`). Separately, OpenCode
scans plugin directories:

| Scope | Directory | Evidence |
|-------|-----------|----------|
| Global | `~/.config/opencode/plugins/` | third-party (envsitter README) |
| Project | `.opencode/plugins/` | third-party (envsitter README) |

OpenCode V1 used the singular `plugin` key and a `server()` export; V2 uses
`plugins` and `setup()`. The envsitter package ships both and says V2 also
accepts the V1 `plugin` key. Treat the directory scan and the V1-key
compatibility as third-party facts until confirmed against the official loader
docs or a live binary.

A plugin that imports only Node built-ins needs no `package.json` or dependency
install next to the file. A plugin that imports `effect` or `@opencode/plugin`
must use the host's copies: the loader rejects imports of those packages from a
plugin's own `node_modules` (`@opencode/plugin` README).

## Hook surface

`ctx` exposes domains, each with `hook(name, callback)` returning a disposable
registration. The callbacks receive one mutable object; mutation is how a plugin
changes behavior, and `tool.execute.before` throws to block.

| Hook | Payload | What a plugin can do |
|------|---------|----------------------|
| `tool.execute.before` | `tool`, `sessionID`, `agent`, `messageID`, `id`, `input` | Inspect or rewrite the tool input; throw to block the call |
| `tool.execute.after` | Same identity plus `status: "completed"` with `result`, or `status: "error"` with `error` | Mutate the result or attach metadata |
| `permission.evaluate` | `sessionID`, optional `agent`, `action`, `resources[]`, `source`, mutable `effect`, mutable `message` | Override the resolved effect, including forcing `deny`, and supply the denial reason |
| `shell.create.before` | `command`, `cwd`, `timeout`, `shell`, `env` | Rewrite or inspect a shell invocation before it is created |
| `session.context` | Request, messages, tools, agent | Change the model request context |
| `session.prompt` / `session.generate` / `session.title` / `session.compaction` | Session request shapes | Change or annotate generated requests |
| `session.model.request` / `http.request` / `http.response` | Provider request or response | Route or inspect model traffic |
| `session.retry` | Error, model, attempt, mutable decision | Change retry behavior |
| `session.experimental.idle` | Background shell/subagent/image work | React before the session goes idle (experimental) |

`tool.transform` edits the tool registry (`add`, `update`, `remove`, namespace).
`skill.transform` and `command.transform` do the same for those registries.
`ctx.event.subscribe()` yields OpenCode events rather than intercepting them.

Two consequences matter for enforcement:

1. `permission.evaluate` is the closest analogue to Claude's `PreToolUse` gate.
   It sees the permission action and the resources the tool checked, and it can
   overwrite `effect` to `deny`. envsitter uses exactly this to block reads,
   edits, and shell commands that name `.env` files, including tool calls made
   from Code Mode (third-party, tested against 2.0.32/2.1.0).
2. `tool.execute.before` sees the parsed tool input, which is what path and
   patch checks need. It is not a permission prompt: throwing produces a tool
   error, not an approval dialog.

The two points are additive, not interchangeable. Use `permission.evaluate` for
logic that must run even when a tool call did not come through the normal
execute path; use `tool.execute.before` when the check needs the concrete input
shape.

## What has no equivalent

- **Claude lifecycle hooks.** OpenCode has session/model hooks, not
  `SessionStart`, `SessionEnd`, `PreCompact`, or notification-style events. A
  plugin can subscribe to events, but it cannot register a per-event command the
  way Claude does.
- **JSON stdin and exit codes.** OpenCode hooks are in-process JavaScript
  callbacks. There is no `exit 2`, no stdout/stderr protocol, and no separate
  hook process. A plugin that wants Claude-like behavior must spawn its own
  checker.
- **Output scrubbing by default.** `tool.execute.after` can rewrite a result,
  but nothing does so unless the plugin implements it. A broad grep can still
  return sensitive file contents before any plugin sees a path.
- **Containment.** A plugin runs with the host user's authority inside the
  OpenCode process. It is a guardrail, not a sandbox.
- **Hook presence gating telemetry.** That behavior is Claude-specific; OpenCode
  telemetry is separate.

## Bridging an external guard

The reusable pattern is a plugin that translates the OpenCode tool input into
whatever an existing checker reads, then maps the result back:

- Shell: `event.tool === "shell"`, command in `input.command`.
- Path tools: `read`, `write`, `edit`, `grep`, `glob`; path fields observed in
  third-party code include `filePath`, `file_path`, `filepath`, `path`,
  `paths`, and `filePaths`.
- Patch: `input.patchText`, with `*** Add File:`, `*** Update File:`,
  `*** Delete File:`, and `*** Move to:` headers plus unified `---`/`+++`
  headers.
- WebFetch: `input.url`; a `file://` URL is worth denying because the read tool
  exists for local files.

A subprocess check must fail in a defined direction. If the interpreter or
module is missing, there is no loader-level default. The rejection path is the
one Claude-style behavior: throw from `tool.execute.before`, or set
`effect = "deny"` and `message` in `permission.evaluate`. The tool call fails,
the model receives the error text, and it can choose another path. Fail-closed
is the only option that gives the model a rejection to react to. Note that
`spawnSync` blocks the event loop for the check's duration.

`console.error` goes to the server log, not the conversation. A non-blocking
warning can be surfaced with
`ctx.session.synthetic({ sessionID, text, delivery, resume })`: it enters the
session inbox and transcript, but it is not a rejection. `resume` defaults to
true and wakes the session; `resume: false` queues the message until the next
wake (`@opencode/core@2.2.7`, `dist/chunks/skill-hr3yjr22.js`). The permission
`message` field is shown only when the evaluated effect is `ask` or `deny`; it
is not a general notification channel.
